name: fb09-pn-plateau-diagnosis
hypothesis: Compressed distinct presynaptic drive is mapped onto a PN count plateau by integration/reset dynamics.
weight_rule: W[post,pre]=budget*count/sum(selected nonself incoming counts); source self-edges masked only in simulator; all cross-side edges retained

encoder.scales: logspace(.005,.05,N_side) in sorted original root-ID order
encoder.assumption: engineered multiscale sensitivity, not measured ORN physiology

gates.propagation: At least one steady-window spike in each intended-side PN, DNa02 and motor group; contralateral activity allowed.
gates.contrast: Right-minus-left DNa02 steady Hz changes in the appropriate direction relative to equal-input bias at each center, by >=1Hz and >=2% of max(total steering Hz,1Hz).
gates.washout: No spikes after 20ms grace; max absolute voltage <1e-4 after 250ms zero input.
gates.stability: Finite voltage throughout, zero-only and pre-pulse baseline silent, maximum per-cell steady-window rate <=250Hz.
gates.causal: All-synapse ablation preserves ORN counts and eliminates all downstream spikes; each DNa02 incoming-edge cut eliminates that DNa02 and its ipsilateral motor spikes, without renormalization.

selection: Run all three candidates; choose the smallest budget passing every pulse gate. No navigation outcomes used.
stop_condition: Stop after three unchanged-parameter replays; no new candidate or training.
seed_reason: Fixed graph, inputs and reset; no random draws.
